title: Legal Personal Assistant
description:
Personal Assistant (Private Client)
- Location: Leatherhead
- Job Type: Full-time
- Salary: £30-£32,000

Join a leading law firm in the Southeast known for its strong history and commitment to client service. We are looking for a Personal Assistant to support our Private Client team, ensuring optimal efficiency and contributing to our tradition of excellence.

Day-to-Day of the Role:
- Provide direct support to a team of four Private Client solicitors/fee earners, alongside two other part-time secretaries.
- Prepare correspondence and documents through audio-typing and word processing.
- Manage daily filing and the maintenance of client files in accordance with office procedures.
- Prepare mail and enclosures for dispatch and handle all copying needs.
- Schedule appointments, arrange meetings, and maintain up-to-date diaries for fee earners.
- Set up and clear conference rooms for meetings and provide refreshments as needed.
- Offer support to other secretaries and provide guidance to junior and temporary secretaries.
- Engage with clients both in person and over the phone in a professional and friendly manner.
- Maintain confidentiality of all firm and client documentation and information.
- Operate the firm's case management system and undertake online form filling requirements.
- Continuously seek to improve the efficiency of the department and undertake additional duties as required.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Substantial previous legal secretarial experience, including at least 2 years in Private Client work.
- Advanced IT skills in relevant packages and fast touch typing skills.
- High levels of accuracy and professionalism in communication.
- Proactive approach to work, able to progress client matters without supervision.
- Ability to work to deadlines, cope under pressure, and effectively prioritise workloads.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, sensitive to the needs of clients during distressing times.
- Demonstrates commitment to the firm and a genuine interest in legal work.

Benefits:
- Competitive salary with annual reviews and bonus schemes.
- 5% employer pension contribution and Death in Service benefit of 4x salary.
- Private medical cover, Life Assurance, and Company sick pay.
- Cycle to Work scheme, Employee Assistance Programme, and Health and Wellbeing initiatives.
- 25 days holiday plus Bank Holidays, with enhanced maternity/paternity leave and other leave benefits.
- Flexible/hybrid working options, sabbaticals, and study leave.
- Comprehensive opportunities for personal and professional development including a Trainee Solicitor Programme and extensive CPD programme.

To apply for this Personal Assistant position, please submit your CV and cover letter detailing your relevant experience and why you are interested in joining to Mark Watts at Reed, your Local Legal Recruitment Manager.

title: Family Support Worker EDT
description:
This role has a starting salary of 17,330 per annum, based on an 18 hour working week (pro rata to 34,660 FTE).

We are recruiting a new Family Support Worker (part time - 18 hours per week) to join our dynamic team at Surrey Emergency Duty Service, part of our CSPA service. Joining the service as a Family Support Worker will be an opportunity to be part of a culture in which children and families are supported in the spirit of partnership that encourages them to develop their own solutions while receiving the help and support they need to address their needs from professionals.

Our Offer to You
- 26 days' holiday (prorated for part-time staff), rising to 28 days after 2 years' service and 31 days after 5 years' service
- Option to buy up to 10 days of additional annual leave
- A generous local government salary related pension
- Up to 5 days of carer's leave and 2 paid volunteering days per year
- Paternity, adoption and dependents leave
- An Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) to support health and wellbeing
- Learning and development hub where you can access a wealth of resources
- Wellbeing and lifestyle discounts including gym, travel, and shopping
- A chance to make a real difference to the lives of our residents

About the Team

The Emergency Duty Team (EDT) operates to respond to emergency situations out of office hours, from 5pm until 9am Monday to Friday, and providing a 24-hour service at weekends and bank holidays (including Christmas).

We respond to critical situations that are unable to wait until the next working day, these relate to children's safeguarding (Section 47), potential placement, or family breakdowns and any other Children's Services related emergency work.

About the Role

Our working environment is outcome focused, you will be working in a fast-paced setting ensuring that cases allocated are resolved in a timely manner and in line with legislation/policies and best practice. The ability to work under pressure and multitask confidently across various IT systems is key to the role.

As an EDT Family Support Worker, you will be responsible for receiving incoming calls and emails and distributing tasks to the appropriate member of staff to respond to. You will be required to undertake visits to family homes, police stations, hospitals etc as the need arises to support children, young people and families in crisis.

We want to be honest with you; the nature of some of the calls and correspondence we receive can be sensitive and at times upsetting. We recognise it can be challenging to take calls about abuse, neglect or from someone who is at risk or in crisis, but it is so important that we provide this service to people who need it. As such, robust personal resilience is essential. You will receive a comprehensive induction program on starting with us; you will receive supervision on a regular basis and will be supported on shift by the Duty Manager in a cohesive and supportive team environment.

Although this role involves working as part of a well-supported team, you will be given the tools to work independently to allow you to deliver work to a high standard.

Shortlisting Criteria

In order to be considered for shortlisting, your application will clearly evidence the following skills and align with our behaviours:
- A sound understanding of social care issues, with a basic awareness of public sector and voluntary agencies
- Experience of working in a social care setting (children or adults)
- Experience of providing high levels of customer care and professionalism in a busy environment
- Able to quickly build rapport and effect successful relationships with customers and partner agencies
- Excellent IT skills and ability to use databases to a high standard of accuracy
- Able to work autonomously with initiative and as part of a team
- Able to travel to Leatherhead and work from home in a confidential space, including access to secure Wi-Fi

An enhanced DBS 'Disclosure and Barring Service' check for regulated activity (formerly known as CRB) and the Children's and Adults' Barred List checks will be required for this role.

The job advert closes at 23:59 on 1st November 2026 with interviews to follow.

Local Government Reorganisation (LGR)

Surrey County Council is undergoing Local Government Reorganisation and will move to new authorities in April 2027. This role is currently employed by Surrey County Council and will remain so until then. If you are employed by Surrey County Council on 1 April 2027, your employment will transfer under TUPE arrangements to one of the new councils, with your current terms and conditions protected. The provisional allocation for this post is East Surrey Council, subject to final confirmation through the wider transition process later this year.

Our Commitment

We are a disability confident employer which means if you have shared a disability on your application form and have evidenced you meet the minimum criteria, we guarantee you an interview.

Your skills and experience truly matter to us. From application to your first day, we're committed to supporting you with any adjustments you need, we value inclusion and warmly welcome you to join and help build a workplace where everyone belongs.

title: Care Assistant - Care Home
description:
ABOUT THE ROLE
As a Care Assistant at a Barchester care home, you'll help residents enjoy each day by making sure they get the quality care and support they deserve. You'll assist with daily living, providing support and companionship and sharing great moments and memories too. It's a chance to bring your dedication and compassion to a fulfilling environment. Every day will be different, so you can expect to undertake work that's as varied as it is rewarding. As a Care Assistant, you could be doing anything from supporting residents with their food and drink and following care plans to ensuring that each of our residents has one-to-one time. It's an opportunity to put your skills to meaningful use and develop your career.

ABOUT YOU
To join us as a Care Assistant you'll need to have some experience of caring for older people, a can-do approach and excellent communication skills. Your empathy and warm-hearted approach will shine through, but above all, you'll have the compassion needed to deliver the highest standard of care and support for all our residents. In return we'll provide all the training you need to thrive.

REWARDS PACKAGE

In return for your dedication, you'll receive a competitive rate of pay plus our sector-leading benefits and rewards package including:

Free training and development for all roles
Access to wellbeing and support tools
A range of retail discounts and savings
Unlimited referrals with our Refer a Friend' bonus scheme
Employee of the Month' rewards and Long Service Awards'

And so much more!

If you'd like to use your people skills in an organisation that provides the quality care you'd expect for your loved ones, this is a rewarding place to be.

title: Home Care Assistant
description:
Home Care Assistant Reigate

Nurse Seekers are currently recruiting a compassionate, reliable, and dedicated Home Care Assistant to support clients in Reigate and the surrounding areas.

This is a fantastic opportunity for individuals with previous care experience who are looking to develop their skills and make a positive impact by helping people maintain their independence and dignity in the comfort of their own homes.

The Role

As a Home Care Assistant, your responsibilities will include:
- Providing personal care and assistance with daily living activities.
- Supporting clients with their individual care needs and routines.
- Assisting with meal preparation and light household tasks where required.
- Offering companionship and emotional support.
- Promoting clients independence, dignity, and overall wellbeing.
- Following care plans and ensuring high standards of care and safeguarding are maintained.

The Ideal Candidate

To be considered for this role, you must:
- Have some previous experience within the care sector.
- Be a driver with a full, valid UK driving licence and have access to reliable transport.
- Have the full right to work in the UK.
- Be compassionate, patient, reliable, and committed to delivering person-centred care.
- Have good communication skills and a genuine passion for supporting others.

Please note: This role is NOT eligible for visa sponsorship. Applicants must already have the full right to work in the UK.

Why Apply?
- The opportunity to make a meaningful difference in people s lives.
- A rewarding role within the home care sector.
- The chance to build on your existing care experience.

Apply Today!

If you have previous care experience, enjoy supporting others, and are looking for your next opportunity in Reigate and the surrounding areas, Nurse Seekers would love to hear from you!

Apply today to find out more about this exciting opportunity.
